title: Pilot governance KPI orchard
content:
Summary:
This working doc is a compact, action-oriented tracker for pilot governance across small-to-medium product launches (beta/pilot waves) and includes a KPI "orchard" (living metric set), phased rollout readiness checks, staffing/coverage schedule, and contingency triggers. Purpose is to give owners (product + ops) a single file they can scan and act on during the 3-week pilot window.

Scope:
- Target launches: feature pilots, dedicated-hosted model rollouts, and early Dedicated capacity customers.
- Not a full go-to-market plan; focus is operational readiness and launch-stability signals.

Success criteria (pilot-level pass/fail):
- Core SLOs met for 7 continuous days at >= 95% of traffic share in the pilot cohort.
- No model-quality regression > 3% on tracked prompt set (see Eval set A).
- Cost-per-1k-token within +/- 20% of forecast for pilot traffic profile.
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) incidents impacting >1% of pilot users < 45 minutes.

KPI orchard (living sheet notes) — primary signals (owners, baseline, target, action threshold):
1) Request throughput (rps) — Owner: Platform Eng — Baseline: 120 rps — Target: 120–250 rps — Action threshold: sustained drop >20% or spike >3x => throttling review (Ops).
2) p50 latency (generation) — Owner: Serving Runtime — Baseline: 180ms — Target: < 220ms — Action threshold: p50 > 350ms (15m window).
3) p95 latency — Owner: Serving Runtime — Baseline: 900ms — Target: <1200ms — Action threshold: p95 > 2s (10m window).
4) Error rate (5xx + client timeouts) — Owner: SRE/Product — Baseline: 0.6% — Target: <1% — Action threshold: >2% sustained 5m => initiate rollback plan.
5) Cache hit rate (prefix/KV) — Owner: Runtime — Baseline: 44% — Target: >55% — Action threshold: <30% for 30m => investigate routing/serving config.
6) Token cost per 1k (USD) — Owner: Product Ops / Finance — Baseline forecast: $1.10 — Target: within +/-20% — Action threshold: >+30% (review quantization / batching).
7) Quality regressions on eval set A (BLEU/ROUGE-like composite) — Owner: Applied ML — Baseline: 0.0% delta — Target: <= +2% improvement or <=3% regression — Action threshold: >3% regression => hold new model.
8) Pilot cohort retention day-1 (D1) — Owner: Growth/Product — Baseline: 18% — Target: >=20% — Action threshold: <12% explore UX/response quality issues.
9) Incidents per 100k requests (severity >=2) — Owner: SRE — Baseline: 0.8 — Target: <1.5 — Action threshold: >3.0 => escalate to CTO forum.

Secondary observability signals (quick checks):
- Model switch/fallback counts (per 1k requests)
- Rate of fallback to smaller model variants
- Autoscale events per hour
- Canary QA mismatch rate (human eval flags)

Phased rollout runway (3 phases, example timeline):
Phase 0 — Preflight (day -7 to -1):
- Run load runbook (PRODOPS-842) on a staging slice that mirrors pilot mix.
- Confirm Dedicated/Hosted routing policies and fallback model variants are configured.
- Run synthetic evals with seed prompts (Applied ML).
- Staff the on-call and have the incident comms template ready.

Phase 1 — Slow-roll (day 0 to day 3):
- Release to 1% of target pilots. Monitor KPI orchard every 15 min.
- Gate: no threshold breaches for 2 consecutive sampling windows.
- If a quality regression >2% triggers, revert model in 10 minutes.

Phase 2 — Ramp (day 4 to day 10):
- Increase traffic by steps (1% -> 5% -> 15% -> 50%) with 4h observation checkpoints.
- Confirm autoscale behaves as expected; monitor cost burn vs forecast.
- Gate: sustained SLO compliance across p95, error rate, and model eval.

Phase 3 — Pilot complete (day 11 to day 21):
- If stable at 50%+ for 7 days, run retrospective and decide to expand to wider cohort or convert to GA plan.

Readiness checklist (quick yes/no items for go/no-go calls):
- [ ] Load test with realistic token distribution completed and within cost forecast.
- [ ] Rollback playbook validated (can revert to previous model within 10m).
- [ ] On-call rota assigned and aware (names + escalation ladder).
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards live and editable by product ops.
- [ ] Access to customer logs and KMS verified for Private deploys.
- [ ] Legal/compliance signoff (for PII-sensitive pilots).
- [ ] Canary eval pass rate >= 95% on small human QA sample.

Staffing & rota (example):
- Primary incident on-call (week): Nora Alvarez (SRE)
- Secondary incident on-call: Samir Patel (Platform Eng)
- Product owner: Priya Kapoor (Product Ops)
- Applied ML point: Elena Ruiz
- Customer success standby (for pilot customers): Jonah Greene
- Escalation to Eng Leadership: Liam O'Connor

Escalation ladder & runbook pointers:
- Level 1 (Investigate): on-call => Slack #pilot-ops, create incident in PagerDuty.
- Level 2 (Mitigate): SRE + Runtime => execute quick rollback or traffic re-route.
- Level 3 (Engage Execs): Product Ops + CTO forum => external comms and decision to pause.

Contingency actions (ordered):
1) Reduce pilot traffic to baseline 5% and enable strict throttling.
2) Switch to fallback smaller model variant that preserves responses but lowers latency/cost.
3) If cost spike: enable aggressive batching and turn on quantization profile B.
4) If quality regression persists: pause rollout and open postmortem with Applied ML and Product.

Post-launch housekeeping and retrospective agenda (7-day post stability):
- Export KPI orchard to a short-run dashboard and snapshot chosen metrics (p95, error rate, cost).
- Annotate any model changes, kernel/quantization updates, or routing policy changes.
- Customer feedback summary: collect the top 5 issues from CS and map to owners.
- Decide: expand to GA path (ops checklist) OR iterate (1–2 week loop).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Should we include a lightweight synthetic regression that targets hallucination risk? (ask Applied ML)
- Confirm whether billing exposure alarms exist for Private (customer-managed) pilots.
- Add a short A/B test slice to compare default vs. cache-warm variant (ticket: PRODOPS-893).

Quick links and artifacts referenced:
- Confluence Pilot Governance Playbook (link above)
- JIRA board: PRODOPS - pilot tickets
- GitHub PR referencing rollback helpers: ops-playbooks/pull/219

Bottom line: this file is the canonical operational checklist + metric watchlist for short pilots. Keep it terse, update the KPI orchard after each roll step, and annotate any threshold breaches with timestamp + owner + action taken.
